passage: Cell biologists in the Petrov laboratory asked whether a metabolic stressor alters transcription of SOD2 in cultured hepatocytes. RNA was extracted from untreated and treated cells, treated with DNase, and reverse transcribed. Quantitative PCR was then performed with primers for SOD2 and for a reference gene whose expression is assumed to be stable. Each reaction contained a fluorescent DNA-binding dye and was run in triplicate. Amplification efficiency was verified to be close to 100% for both primer pairs, meaning the amount of product doubles each cycle. The cycle threshold, Ct, is the cycle at which fluorescence crosses a fixed threshold; mean values are shown. The group planned to calculate relative expression using the comparative Ct method before deciding whether to examine the promoter region for regulatory elements. RNA integrity numbers exceeded 8.5 for every sample. All procedures followed the laboratory's standard operating protocols, and raw data were archived before analysis.

questions.stem: Which condition shows greater starting amounts of SOD2 transcript, based on Table 1?

options.C: The data cannot be compared without a standard curve

questions.explanation: A lower Ct means the threshold is reached earlier, indicating more starting template. With equal reference Ct, the condition with the lower target Ct has higher expression.
questions.trap: Reading a higher Ct as higher expression; a lower Ct means the threshold was reached sooner, so more starting template.

questions.stem: Which control best rules out amplification of contaminating genomic DNA?

options.C: A reaction with double the template
options.D: A reaction run at a higher annealing temperature only

questions.explanation: If product appears without reverse transcriptase, it must come from DNA rather than from RNA-derived cDNA.
questions.trap: Omitting the no-reverse-transcriptase control, so amplification of genomic DNA could be mistaken for cDNA signal.

questions.stem: Using the ΔΔCt method with 100% efficiency, what is the fold change in SOD2 in treated versus untreated cells?
questions.trap: Using 2^(+ΔΔCt) instead of 2^(−ΔΔCt), or forgetting to normalize the target Ct to the reference gene.

questions.stem: Which statement about Ct values is INCORRECT?

options.A: A lower Ct indicates a higher starting amount of target
options.B: The reference gene corrects for differences in input RNA
options.C: A higher Ct indicates a higher starting amount of target
options.D: A difference of one Ct corresponds to a two-fold difference at 100% efficiency

questions.explanation: Ct and abundance are inversely related; more template reaches threshold sooner.
questions.trap: Equating a higher Ct with more starting transcript; Ct is the cycle at which signal crosses threshold, so a lower Ct means more template.

questions.stem: If expression changes, which feature of the gene would most directly be examined for a transcription-factor response?

options.A: The poly-A tail of the mature mRNA only
options.B: The anticodon of the matching tRNA
options.C: The number of introns within the coding region only
options.D: Promoter and enhancer sequences upstream of the transcription start site

questions.explanation: Transcription-factor binding sites (promoter/enhancer elements) govern transcriptional initiation, linking the Ct data to the regulatory mechanism.
questions.trap: Looking for the regulatory effect in the poly-A tail, introns or tRNA instead of the promoter and enhancer sequences that control initiation.
